The Help of God (Ebenezer)
thuh HELP uhv GOD (EB-uh-NEE-zur)
noun (divine provision)
From Hebrew eben ha-ezer, the stone of help (1 Sam 7:12); help from Old English help, succor or aid rendered in need.

📖 Biblical Definition

The help of God is His timely and effectual succor of His people in their need, the strong arm by which He upholds, delivers, and sustains those who call upon Him. When the LORD had routed the Philistines, "Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Eben-ezer, saying, Hitherto hath the LORD helped us" (1 Sam 7:12). The stone was a memorial, a heaped witness that all the way thus far was paved with mercy. The psalmist makes this help a refuge in calamity: "God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble" (Psa 46:1), and again, "My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth" (Psa 121:2). Such help is not a vague optimism but the concrete intervention of a covenant God who hears, defends, and provides. The remembrance of past mercies is itself a means of grace, for the saint who counts up his Ebenezers is fortified against present fear and future doubt. This dictionary confesses that the people of God are kept not by their own strength but by His ready help, and that gratitude for mercies received is the proper soil of faith for mercies yet to come.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The help of God is His timely succor of His people, memorialized in Samuel's stone Ebenezer. He is a very present help in trouble. The remembrance of past mercies strengthens faith for the future.

expand to see more

HELP OF GOD, noun. The effectual aid and succor God renders His people in their time of need.

It was memorialized by Samuel in the stone Ebenezer, a witness that the LORD had helped His people thus far.

"God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble" (Psa 46:1).

It requires that we call upon Him and remember His mercies; it forbids the self-reliance that forgets the Giver.

It is the ground of confidence that He who has helped will help still, even unto the end.

📖 Key Scripture

1 Sam 7:12 — "Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Eben-ezer, saying, Hitherto hath the LORD helped us."

Psa 46:1 — "God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble."

Psa 121:2 — "My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth."

Heb 13:6 — "So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The age trades the help of a personal, covenant God for self-help, positive thinking, and the autonomous self as its own savior.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Yet the spirit of the age quietly replaces the help of God with the gospel of self-reliance, where a man looks within for strength and counts his deliverances as the fruit of his own resolve. Such pride forgets the Giver and leaves the soul without refuge when its own strength fails.

Recover the practice of the Ebenezer: heap up the memorials of mercy and say with Samuel, "Hitherto hath the LORD helped us." The saint who remembers past help is armed against present fear, for the God who has been a very present help in trouble does not change. Gratitude looks back upon mercy and so looks forward with faith.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word Ebenezer joins Hebrew eben, stone, to ezer, help, naming the LORD as the helper of His people.

expand to see more

Hebrew eben, stone, supplies the first half of Ebenezer, the memorial Samuel raised.

Hebrew ezer, help, is the same word used of the help God Himself supplies in Psa 121:2.

The clause ad-hennah, "hitherto," marks the backward look over a path of mercy.

Old English help gives our word, succor rendered to one in need.

Heb 13:6 carries the same confession into the new covenant, "The Lord is my helper."

Usage

"She raised her own Ebenezer after the long illness, confessing that hitherto the LORD had helped her."

"In the worst of the trouble he clung to Psalm 46, that God is a very present help."

"The help of God, not his own contriving, had carried the family through the lean years."
